text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Uterine tenderness. I also have Decreased bowel sounds, Increased frequency of urination, Fever. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand your urgency; please wait for the CBC, CRP, and blood culture results to guide us. Given your uterine tenderness, decreased bowel sounds, and fever, did your uterus ever feel firm during your postpartum check-ups, or has it remained boggy?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Uncomplicated pregnancy leading up to a vaginal delivery. No significant past medical or surgical history. Social history: Does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. Lives with her partner.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history; since you are not breastfeeding, is your breast milk coming in normally? I am particularly concerned about your decreased bowel sounds alongside the fever; have you had any episodes of vomiting or been unable to pass gas since delivery? REQUEST TEST: Lactate, Amylase

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your decreased bowel sounds and the urgency you've expressed, have you been passing gas or having any bowel movements since delivery? Also, did the pain start immediately after the baby was born or develop later? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_CT_with_contrast. DIAGNOSIS READY: Postpartum Pelvic Inflammatory Disease with possible pelvic abscess formation.
